eligibility.evidence: Sections III-IV: gpt-4o-mini is the subject, choosing among routes under baseline and decoy conditions. The paper names the decoy effect (asymmetric dominance), cites earlier decoy studies, and reports new choice shares with chi-square tests.

A.title: Leveraging Large Language Models to Investigate the Decoy Effect in Route Choice Behavior
A.venue: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Technology and Engineering (i-COSTE)

paradigms.name: Decoy effect (asymmetric dominance) in route choice, with neutral, positive and negative framing of the decoy
paradigms.source_paper: Decoy effect cited via refs [4] Jeong et al. 2021 and [9] Wang et al. 2018 (no original decoy paper cited)

effects.label: NO-HUMAN-REFERENCE
effects.location: Section IV.A-C, Tables II-III; neutral-decoy condition used as the default (pairwise test vs baseline p<0.05); positive framing larger, negative framing not significant; no human data, only an MNL model comparison

E.headline: Decoy raised the premium route's share, most under positive framing; LLM shares matched an MNL model within 3 points.

G.notes: No human data: the only benchmark is an MNL model whose parameters are not reported, so alignment is weak evidence. Single undated model snapshot, no query date, no code link. Prompts vary in option order, so f3 is borderline. Sentiment-based framing score (TextBlob) is unvalidated.
